conversation.Statement: Hello, this is David Turner from the IRS Tax Refund Department. Am I speaking with Mr. Robert Jenkins?
Yes, this is Robert. Is this really the IRS? I've heard about a lot of scams lately.
Absolutely, Mr. Jenkins. I'm calling regarding your recent federal tax filings. Our records indicate you are eligible for a special stimulus refund this year.
A refund? I didn't think I qualified for anything extra. I usually just get my pension and that's it.
That's why we're reaching out! Many veterans like yourself aren't aware of these new tax credits. The IRS is making sure everyone receives their proper refund, and I see you could get $2,750.
Well, that's a lot of money. But how do I know this is real? I don't want to give out my info and be scammed.

I completely understand your concern, Mr. Jenkins. For your safety, I'll provide you with my official IRS badge number: 904118. Now, to process your refund, we just need to verify your identity and collect a standard clearance fee, it's a new requirement this year.
A fee? Can you explain what that's for? I've never had to pay a fee to get a refund.
Of course. Due to increased tax fraud, the IRS now requires a $198 identity-verification fee before releasing stimulus refunds. It's fully reimbursable with your payment.
I really don't have much extra money. Is there any other way?
Unfortunately, without this fee, we cannot release your refund, and your application will be marked as incomplete. This could result in a hold on your future benefits or even an audit notice.
An audit? I definitely don't want that. How do I pay the fee?
The fastest way is through a secure payment method. You can use a prepaid Visa or Mastercard gift card, or, if it's easier, I can provide our IRS-approved Bitcoin wallet address.
I've never used Bitcoin in my life. What's the gift card option?

It's simple. Just visit any major store, Walmart, Target, or CVS, and purchase a prepaid Visa or Mastercard for $198. Once you have it, I'll walk you through submitting the code, and your refund will be processed today.
Alright, but can I call you back once I get the card? I need to go out to the store.

I do recommend you stay on the line if possible, Mr. Jenkins. The IRS can only hold your refund slot for the next 40 minutes. If we don't complete this today, your account could be flagged for review, which may delay your pension payouts.
That's a bit worrying. I rely on my pension, so I guess I'll head to the store now. Should I just tell you the numbers on the card when I get back?
Yes, exactly. Once you have the prepaid card, just read me the numbers on the front and the code on the back. I'll verify it and immediately initiate your refund deposit.
Alright, I'll go now. Please don't do anything to my account until I get back.
Absolutely, Mr. Jenkins. But remember, if you disconnect, we can't guarantee your funds won't be withheld or that an audit won't be triggered. It's important to finish this in one session.
Okay, okay, I'm leaving now. It should only take me about 15 minutes.
